topics.title: The French Revolution and liberal nationalism

outcomes.statement: Explains how the French Revolution and the Napoleonic Code spread the idea of the nation across Europe.
Describes liberal nationalism and the revolutions of 1848, including what the middle classes demanded.

topics.title: The making of Germany and Italy

outcomes.statement: Describes the unification of Germany under Bismarck and of Italy under Mazzini, Cavour and Garibaldi.
Explains how romantic imagination, allegory and culture such as Greek independence helped create national feeling.
Explains why the Balkans became a source of nationalist tension after 1871, and how nationalism became linked with imperialism.

concepts.name: The French Revolution and liberal nationalism

topics.title: The First World War, Khilafat and Non-Cooperation

outcomes.statement: Explains why the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre outraged Indians.
Describes how different social groups — towns, peasants in Awadh, tribals in the Gudem Hills, plantation workers — joined the Non-Cooperation Movement.
Identifies and labels Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad, Jallianwala Bagh and the 1920 Congress sessions at Calcutta and Nagpur on an outline map of India.

topics.title: Civil Disobedience and a sense of collective belonging

outcomes.statement: Describes the Salt March and the Civil Disobedience Movement, including the Simon Commission and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
Explains the limits of the Civil Disobedience Movement for Dalits and Muslims.
Explains how history, folklore, images and symbols such as the flag built a sense of collective belonging.
Identifies and labels Dandi and the 1927 Madras session of the Congress on an outline map of India.

topics.title: The pre-modern and nineteenth-century world economy

outcomes.statement: Describes the pre-modern links of trade, such as the silk routes and the exchange of food crops.
Explains how the world economy took shape in the nineteenth century, including the role of technology such as refrigerated ships and of colonialism.
Explains the causes of the Great Depression and why agricultural regions were hit hardest.
Describes the post-war international economic order, including the Bretton Woods institutions.

concepts.name: The Great Depression and the post-war economy

outcomes.statement: Explains proto-industrialisation and the role of cities such as London as finishing centres.
Explains why hand labour persisted in Victorian Britain, and why women spinners attacked the Spinning Jenny.
Describes what happened to Indian weavers under colonial rule, including the effect of the American Civil War.
Explains the growth of Indian factories, early entrepreneurs and the effect of the First World War on Indian industry.

topics.title: Print in China, Japan and Europe

outcomes.statement: Describes the early history of print in China and Japan, and Gutenberg's press in Europe.
Explains how print created a reading public and helped bring about the Reformation and the French Revolution, and why the Church censored books.
Describes how print came to India and how it spread religious reform and debate.
Explains how print created new readers among women, workers and the lower castes, and how the colonial state censored it.

concepts.name: The print revolution in the world
